scene: The morning after the crossing. Antony and Quintus Cassius climb out of a hired carriage in slaves' tunics and Caesar shows them to the army as they are
what_changes: Antony becomes the reason the army gives itself for the war; he feels the ranks decide
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar has marched on Italy; the tribunes of the people were driven out of Rome, or say they were
pov_lens: Notices the ranks' faces and his own bare legs; misreads the roar as love for him; hides that the tunic was his idea of a joke

place: Rome: the house on the Sacred Way
scene: Pompey and the consuls have left Rome. The street empties of litters; Phileros bars the door at noon; Calpurnia sends to her father's
what_changes: The household learns it is the house of the enemy of the men who own Rome, and nobody tells the kitchen what to do
reader_knows_by_end: Rome has been abandoned to Caesar without a fight; Calpurnia's house is Caesar's house
pov_lens: Notices the oil jars and who has gone home to their families; misreads the quiet as safety; hides a lamp she should not have lit. Chreste sleeps next to her

scene: The Kalends of February. Nobody borrows, nobody pays, senators have gone with their cash. Visellius comes and counts his interest out in stacks of ten
what_changes: Hordeonius's trade of thirty years, election loans, stops; he must find a new security
reader_knows_by_end: Credit has frozen in Rome; Visellius is a man who pays
pov_lens: Notices whose stewards did not come; misreads the freeze as a week's panic; hides from Sosia that he has no buyer for any paper on the board

scene: His legion comes down from Gaul and catches up in Picenum, his own country. Cingulum, Labienus's town, opens its gates; Labienus has gone to Pompey
what_changes: Laberius learns the war runs through his own valley and that men he knew by sight in Gaul are on the other side
reader_knows_by_end: Labienus, Caesar's right hand in Gaul, has changed sides; Picenum is Pompey's country
pov_lens: Notices Picene water jars, a dialect word, Labienus's empty house; misreads the open gates as welcome; hides that he is home and does not go up the valley

scene: Cicero, with his lictors and their laurelled fasces and no triumph, writes letters about which side to be ashamed of
what_changes: Cicero commits to nothing and finds the laurels have become a joke he must walk past every morning
reader_knows_by_end: Cicero is between the sides; he was promised a triumph that will now not happen
pov_lens: Notices sentences in the letters he gets; misreads Pompey's flight as strategy; hides from Tiro that he is waiting to be asked

scene: The siege of seven days. Domitius's soldiers give him up. Caesar sends Domitius and the senators away unharmed and gives Domitius back his money
what_changes: Laberius watches men he has been told are enemies go free with their silver, and Picene levies from Domitius's army sworn into Caesar's
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar pardons his enemies on principle; the soldiers who were enemies are now in his army
pov_lens: Notices the senators' shoes and the silver chests; misreads the pardon as a gentlemen's custom that costs the soldiers nothing; hides his anger about the silver in a joke Vibius tells for him

scene: Brutus, serving with Sestius, gets Caesar's Corfinium letter in a copy and decides to go to Pompey, the man who had his father put to death
what_changes: Brutus chooses the side of the man he hates because it is the side of the law, and is courteous to everyone about it
reader_knows_by_end: Brutus's father was killed on Pompey's orders; Brutus goes to him anyway
pov_lens: Notices what is fitting and the copy of the letter in a clerk's hand; misreads his decision as uncomplicated; hides that the kindness in Caesar's letter moved him

scene: Caesar comes to see Cicero and asks him to come to Rome and speak for peace. Cicero refuses, politely; Caesar says he will have to take advice where he can
what_changes: Cicero has refused Caesar to his face; he is proud of it and frightened by it
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar wants respectable men in Rome; Cicero will not be one
pov_lens: Notices Caesar's courtesy as a performance he admires; misreads the refusal as costless; hides from himself how much he wanted to say yes

scene: Caesar takes the treasury. The tribune Metellus stands in the door; Caesar threatens him; Antony carries the order out and finds he likes the noise
what_changes: Antony is given Italy to hold while Caesar goes to Spain
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar has the state's money and has used force on a tribune, the thing the war was said to be about
pov_lens: Notices the crowd going quiet and the smiths at the doors; misreads the silence as consent; hides that he saw the irony and laughed
sources: Caes. BC 1.32 to 33; Plut. Caes. 35; App. BC 2.41 (check)

scene: The treasury's coin goes out to the army through the Forum. A debtor offers Hordeonius a farm in place of money; nobody can say what a farm is worth this month
what_changes: Hordeonius takes land as security for the first time in years and dislikes the feel of it
reader_knows_by_end: Coin is scarce and land has no price; the army is being paid
pov_lens: Notices the mint marks and the farm's boundary stones on a tablet; misreads land as the safe asset; hides his dislike behind a proverb for Sosia

scene: Curio leaves for Sicily and Africa. Antony comes to see him off and meets Curio's wife, Fulvia, managing the house and the creditors
what_changes: Antony sees what Fulvia does when the husband is not in the room
reader_knows_by_end: Curio is Caesar's, bought with his debts paid; Fulvia was Clodius's widow before she was Curio's wife
pov_lens: Notices Fulvia's keys and the creditors' boys at the gate; misreads her as Curio's business; hides that he envies Curio the house

scene: Cicero sails to join Pompey. Tullia, married to Dolabella, who is with Caesar, sees him off; Terentia sends money short
what_changes: Cicero has chosen, and the choice puts his daughter's husband on the other side
reader_knows_by_end: Cicero's family is split across the war; Dolabella is Caesar's man
pov_lens: Notices what Tullia does not say; misreads her calm as courage; hides that he chose the side that would think better of him

scene: Floods take the bridges; grain is short and dear in Caesar's camp; Laberius cannot swim
what_changes: Laberius learns that hunger and the river can beat the army before Afranius does
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar's army in Spain is in trouble
pov_lens: Notices the water line on the stakes and who is eating; misreads the river as the enemy; hides that he cannot swim by finding work on the bank

scene: The armies meet across the lines and ask after men from their towns. A big slow Picene in Afranius's army knows Laberius's valley. Petreius has the visitors killed; Caesar sends Afranius's men back unharmed. The Picene comes over
what_changes: Rufrius takes the next tent (proposal; Book 1 says only 'since Ilerda')
reader_knows_by_end: Pompeian and Caesarian soldiers are the same men from the same towns; the generals keep them apart
pov_lens: Notices the Picene's empty-handed way of arriving with wine; misreads the fraternising as the end of the war; hides that he watched the killings and did nothing

place: Rome: the house on the Sacred Way
scene: News comes by letter and by street: Massilia's fleet beaten by Decimus Brutus, Spain going well. The house buys oil and wool for a long war
what_changes: Nysa learns the house's fortunes rise and fall with letters she cannot read fast enough
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar is winning in the west; Decimus Brutus is his man at sea
pov_lens: Notices which letters make Calpurnia eat; misreads good news as the end; hides from Chreste that she can read a little

scene: Brutus arrives; Pompey rises and embraces him. Brutus works at his epitome of Polybius in his tent while the camp talks about what Caesar's men will be given
what_changes: Brutus is welcomed by the man he hates and finds the welcome easy to take
reader_knows_by_end: Pompey's side expects to win and is already dividing the spoils
pov_lens: Notices Pompey's courtesy and the officers' boredom with books; misreads his own coolness as principle; hides that he liked the embrace

scene: News that Curio is dead at the Bagradas, his head sent to Juba. Antony goes to the house; Fulvia has buried two husbands
what_changes: Antony learns what Africa does to Caesar's men, and stays longer at the house than he needs to
reader_knows_by_end: Curio is dead; Fulvia is a widow for the second time
pov_lens: Notices her hands at the household's books; misreads her composure as coldness; hides why he came
sources: Caes. BC 2.38 to 42; App. BC 2.45 to 46

scene: The Ninth mutinies for the five minae a man promised at Brundisium. Caesar threatens decimation, takes 120, executes 12 by lot. One of the twelve is absent, and the centurion who named him dies in his place
what_changes: Laberius sees a centurion pay for a man of his; he learns what a promise of money is worth and what asking for it costs
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar's soldiers were promised money and are being made to wait; he punishes asking
pov_lens: Notices the lots and the absent man's empty place; misreads the executions as about discipline; hides his own share of the grumbling from the tribunes

scene: Caesar is dictator for eleven days. Arbitrators value property at what it was worth before the war; Hordeonius must take a debtor's farm at a price nobody would pay now
what_changes: Hordeonius loses money to a law for the first time and admires its drafting
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar's debt law protects debtors without cancelling debts; creditors lose
pov_lens: Notices the arbitrator's seal and the debtor's relief; misreads the law as the end of the matter; hides his loss in the ledger as 'valued'

place: Rome: the house on the Sacred Way
scene: Caesar's eleven days at home. The house doubles its lamps. Nysa carries water past the master's door and he asks her name and forgets it. A thin boy of fourteen in the family party is ignored by everyone
what_changes: The house has seen its master and he has gone again, to Brundisium and the sea
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar is consul for 48 and crossing to Greece; his family includes a boy nobody notices
pov_lens: Notices the master's sandals and the boy's thin shoes; misreads the master's notice as favour; hides that she said her name twice

scene: Cicero in the camp, ill and making jokes nobody forgives. Cato is there. Brutus is courteous
what_changes: Cicero learns the side he joined does not want him
reader_knows_by_end: Pompey's camp is confident, quarrelsome and short of patience with Cicero
pov_lens: Notices who laughs at his jokes and who repeats them; misreads the coldness as envy; hides that he wants to go home

scene: Antony brings the rest of the army across a sea Pompey's fleet holds. A storm, a lucky wind, a harbour; recruits on a captured ship killed after a promise of safety
what_changes: Antony has done the hardest thing in the campaign and done it well
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar's army is now together in Greece
pov_lens: Notices the men's sickness and the sail-handling; misreads luck as skill and knows it; hides fear in noise

scene: Months of digging. The men make bread from chara root and throw loaves over to the Pompeians; Pompey hides them from his army
what_changes: Laberius is proud of the root bread; the army is starving and digging
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar is besieging a bigger army; his men are hungrier than the men they besiege
pov_lens: Notices the bread's crust and the Pompeians' horses dying; misreads hunger as a contest he is winning; hides his own hunger from his century
sources: Caes. BC 3.48; App. BC 2.61; Suet. Jul. 68 (check)

scene: Caelius sets up his chair beside Trebonius's and offers debtors six years without interest, then cancellation. Debtors queue. Visellius does not
what_changes: Hordeonius sees a praetor offer to make his paper worthless
reader_knows_by_end: Debt is the politics of Rome while the armies are away; Trebonius holds the line for Caesar
pov_lens: Notices who queues at Caelius's chair and who does not; misreads Caelius as a fool; hides relief when Visellius pays

place: Rome: the house on the Sacred Way
scene: Caelius's riots, Milo's return, the Senate's decree. Then news that Caesar has been beaten at Dyrrachium, or killed, or both. The house waits
what_changes: Nysa sees the house's fear for the first time in Calpurnia's face; the false news of his death goes through the kitchen
reader_knows_by_end: Caelius and Milo are dead; Caesar has had a defeat; rumour gets there first
pov_lens: Notices Calpurnia's nails and the steward's lists; misreads rumour as news; hides her own relief at being alive

scene: Pompey breaks the lines. Standards lost; men run; afterwards the men ask to be punished
what_changes: Laberius has run. The army is beaten and moves east
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar has lost at Dyrrachium and goes into Thessaly
pov_lens: Notices the lost standard's empty socket and whose feet ran; misreads Caesar's calm as anger; hides that he ran

scene: Before the battle. Pompey's officers quarrel over Caesar's priesthood and who will have which office. Brutus reads
what_changes: Brutus sees his side divide a victory it has not won and says nothing
reader_knows_by_end: Pompey's side is sure of winning
pov_lens: Notices the officers' voices and his own page; misreads his silence as detachment; hides contempt

scene: The battle from the left wing, in pieces. Antony holds; he does not see the cavalry broken on the other wing; he sees only that it is over
what_changes: Antony has commanded a wing in the battle that decides the war
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar has won; Pompey has fled
pov_lens: Notices bodies and noise and a horse's mouth; misreads the end as his; hides nothing

scene: The Pompeian camp with tables laid and tents hung with myrtle, silver on the boards. Domitius killed running
what_changes: Laberius has been in a battle won; he sees what the other side had for dinner and the pardoned man dead
reader_knows_by_end: Domitius, pardoned at Corfinium, fought again and died
pov_lens: Notices the silver and Domitius's shoes, the same as at Corfinium; misreads the tables as an insult; hides that he takes a cup

scene: Through the marsh to Larissa, mud to the knees, a letter to Caesar. Caesar is glad, has him in, gives him dinner, puts a hand on his shoulder. He sounds Brutus on where Pompey has gone; Brutus guesses Egypt. Brutus tries to soften him towards Cassius. Caesar writes to Servilia that night
what_changes: Brutus is pardoned and has given Caesar the direction of Pompey's flight
reader_knows_by_end: Brutus is spared and grateful, and hates being grateful
pov_lens: Notices the dinner's courtesy and the weight of a hand; misreads his answer about Egypt as conversation; hides from himself the gladness

scene: Cicero lands at Brundisium, with his lictors still, and waits for Caesar's word
what_changes: Cicero is out of the war and not yet forgiven
reader_knows_by_end: Cicero left Pompey's side after Pharsalus and is waiting on Caesar
pov_lens: Notices the harbour's watchers; misreads waiting as decency; hides the lictors in a back room

place: Rome: the house on the Sacred Way; the Forum
scene: News that Pompey is dead in Egypt. Statues come down. The thin boy takes the toga of manhood with the family; the house sends linen
what_changes: Nysa sees the war decided in a city that did not fight it
reader_knows_by_end: Pompey has been killed on landing in Egypt; Caesar is in Alexandria
pov_lens: Notices the statues' plinths and the boy's new toga, too big; misreads the end of the war; hides that Chreste's joke about it was funny
sources: Caes. BC 3.104; Plut. Pomp. 79 to 80; Dio 42.18; Nic. Dam. Aug. 4 (check)

place: Rome: the Master of the Horse's house
scene: Antony governs Italy for an absent dictator. He signs the edict that keeps Pompeians out and names Cicero as excepted. Cytheris; a wife he suspects
what_changes: Antony has power with nobody watching and spends it on noise
reader_knows_by_end: Antony is Caesar's deputy in Rome; Caesar is stuck in Alexandria
pov_lens: Notices his guests' laughter; misreads it as loyalty; hides the suspicion about Dolabella and his wife

scene: Dolabella proposes cancelling debts and rents. Bucco is at the Janus as Antony's man. Visellius pays
what_changes: Hordeonius sees a tribune who is Caesar's own man offer to cancel his paper, and Antony's agent setting up beside him
reader_knows_by_end: Dolabella is Caesar's man and Antony's rival; debt is again the politics of Rome
pov_lens: Notices Bucco's stool and Antony's seal; misreads Antony as the creditor's friend; hides that Dolabella owes him

scene: Tullia comes to her father. Her marriage is going bad; Dolabella's debt laws are the talk of Rome. A letter comes from Caesar, or does not
what_changes: Cicero sees what his choices have cost his daughter
reader_knows_by_end: Tullia is married to Dolabella and unhappy; Cicero is still waiting
pov_lens: Notices her laugh and what it is at; misreads her visit as consolation; hides from her that he is waiting for her husband's master

scene: Brutus speaks before Caesar for King Deiotarus. Caesar listens and says afterwards that what Brutus wants he wants very much
what_changes: Brutus has learned he can ask Caesar for things
reader_knows_by_end: Brutus is Caesar's favourite of the pardoned
pov_lens: Notices the king's age and his own sentences; misreads being heard as being equal; hides the warmth

scene: Dolabella's day: barricades and wooden towers in the Forum. Antony brings soldiers down from the Capitol at dawn and cuts down the tablets of the laws; men are thrown from the Capitol. The house bars its doors
what_changes: Nysa has seen soldiers kill citizens in the Forum within sight of the house
reader_knows_by_end: Antony has put down Dolabella with soldiers
pov_lens: Notices the towers' timber and the steward's count of who is in; misreads soldiers as protection; hides Chreste, who was out

scene: Caesar lands. Cicero goes out to meet him. Caesar gets down, embraces him and walks with him alone for a long way
what_changes: Cicero is forgiven, and it is easy, and that is the worst of it
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar pardons Cicero in person
pov_lens: Notices the road dust and Caesar's ease; misreads the walk as friendship; hides relief

scene: The legions in Campania will not sail again without what they were promised. Sallust nearly killed, two senators killed. They march on Rome
what_changes: Laberius marches with the mutiny and does not lead it
reader_knows_by_end: The soldiers want discharge and the money and land promised
pov_lens: Notices the plain by the Volturnus from the road, good ground; misreads the march as a way to be paid; hides that he looked at the land

scene: The sale of Pompey's goods. Antony buys the house. Hordeonius knows he will not pay
what_changes: Pompey's house has a new owner and an unpaid price
reader_knows_by_end: Antony owns Pompey's house; nobody expects the money
pov_lens: Notices the bidders and the auction spear; misreads Antony's credit as Caesar's; hides that he lent the auctioneer's clerk money

scene: Caesar is back and cold to him. Antony is asked to pay for the house and is indignant. Dolabella is pardoned and honoured. Fulvia
what_changes: Antony is out of favour and takes the one ally who does not need Caesar
reader_knows_by_end: Antony has lost Caesar's favour; he will marry Fulvia
pov_lens: Notices Fulvia's keys again; misreads Caesar's coldness as passing; hides the humiliation in a party

scene: Caesar comes out to the mutineers and calls them Quirites, citizens. They beg to serve. He promises land from public holdings and his own, settled apart so no owner is put out, part of the money now and the rest later. Laberius asks a clerk for the day. The scar-lipped man of the Tenth is near. Last scene
what_changes: Laberius has a promise of land and no date
reader_knows_by_end: Caesar has promised land without taking anyone's; nobody has said when
pov_lens: Notices the clerk's tablet and the scar-lipped man's spit; misreads the promise as a date that will follow; hides that he begged with the rest
